assessment.support_scope: EuroQol Research Foundation award 1850-RA: "http://dx.doi.org/10.13039/501100006419EuroQol Research Foundation 1850-RA".
assessment.reason: This protocol makes the experimental EQ-TIPS-5L descriptive system a primary research object. It plans to test whether its severity levels agree with preferences, whether its attribute levels affect choices, and whether kaizen tasks and paired comparisons give consistent evidence. The structured funding statement identifies direct EuroQol Research Foundation support for the work.

studies.label: Two-wave Australian DCE assessment of the EQ-TIPS-5L descriptive system
studies.family_rationale: The intended main results concern the performance of the EQ-TIPS-5L descriptive system: severity-preference concordance and whether its attribute levels have non-zero effects on choices. The study also compares valuation tasks, but it does not state that a revised instrument version or value set will be its principal output.

items.label: kaizen tasks
profiles: Profiles formed by applying one possible attribute-level change to the current profile
Four good changes and one bad change in each task
levels: Five EQ-TIPS-5L severity levels: no problems or no pain, a little bit, some, a lot, and extreme
items.duration: A 1-month episode starting today for a 1-year-old child, followed by recovery
items.alternatives: Five possible changes at the first choice, followed by four, three, and two remaining changes as the profile is updated
items.task_count: 14 kaizen tasks per respondent, plus a warm-up task
items.block: Two d-efficient blocks of 14 origin-destination pairs; planned target of 200 respondents per block
items.order: EQ-TIPS-5L attribute order will be randomized at respondent level, and task sequence will be randomized within each component.
items.randomization_unit: Respondent for attribute order; task sequence within respondent
items.stopping_rule: The process continues until four of five possible changes are incorporated; the unselected change is ranked fifth.

items.statement: Paired comparisons require choices between profiles of health problems and are more burdensome than kaizen tasks, especially when choices affect the health of a 1-year-old child.

items.label: type-1 and type-2 discordance
items.description: Type-1 discordance occurs when a bad change is selected before the end of a kaizen task; type-2 discordance occurs when an improvement is not selected and is ranked fifth.
